chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q2 — Sampling and Experimental Design (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Statistics FRQ 2 focuses on Sampling and Experimental Design, 4 points. Each lettered part is scored E/P/I and combined into an integer 0–4. Typical tasks: identify a sampling method or bias, describe how to implement random assignment/selection, explain the purpose of a control or of random assignment (to allow cause-and-effect / reduce confounding), and identify the scope of inference. Common failure: describing randomization vaguely (not replicable); confusing random sampling (generalizability) with random assignment (causation); stating the purpose of a design feature without the statistical reason.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q2 scored 4/4 — all parts essentially correct: a replicable randomization description, the correct statistical purpose of the design feature, and the correct scope of inference. Full-credit model for the design question.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2B, 3/4
chunks.content: Q2 scored 3/4 — most parts correct with one partial, commonly a randomization description missing a replicable detail or a purpose stated without the full statistical reasoning. Illustrates a strong response one part short.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q2 scored 1/4 — mostly incorrect/partial: vague randomization, or confusing random sampling with random assignment, and missing the design feature's purpose. Illustrates weak command of sampling/experimental-design principles.
